clue.text: Duty to chase wrong-sounding grammatical structure

indicators.note: to chase is to come behind, so the duty word follows the other piece
the word 'sounding' tied to 'wrong' says we want a word that sounds like a word for wrong, not its spelling

parts.note: a wrong or misdeed is a sin
a duty is a levy or tax

explanation.surface: A grammar note: a tax that pursues an ill-sounding construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong-sounding' gives SYN, said like SIN; 'to chase' puts TAX after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the arrangement of words into sentences, a grammatical structure.

clue.text: Textile worker's rank

parts.note: serge is a woven fabric
a worker is a type of ant

explanation.surface: A textile worker's position in the hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; 'worker' is the crossword ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned military rank above corporal.

clue.text: New troubles mean arrests

parts.note: to trouble someone is to ail them

explanation.surface: Fresh problems mean people are taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a suspect is informal for catching or arresting them.

clue.text: Asian chap, a fellow I hang around

indicators.note: around suggests moving the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: An Asian man describes himself as a fellow who loiters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I HANG to GHANI.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afghani is a native of Afghanistan, an Asian country.

clue.text: Block letters in Times covering the end of poverty

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the single letter taken from poverty
the clue treats the letters in the word Times as material to be rearranged
the last letter of the word poverty is the one taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper's block letters obscure the final point about poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters in' rearranges TIMES to STMIE; 'covering' puts Y, from 'the end of poverty', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stymie is to obstruct or thwart, so block works as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Work ultimately missing from development of upmarket Japanese course

indicators.note: development turns the letters of upmarket into a new form, minus the missing letter
ultimately points to the last letter of the word Work

explanation.surface: Dishes for a posh Japanese meal lack finishing work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives K from Work; 'missing from' and 'development of' rearrange UPMARKET without that K.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is battered, deep-fried Japanese food served as a course.

clue.text: Choppers initially used to exploit real power

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
a law with teeth has real power to enforce it

explanation.surface: Young teeth first used to take advantage of genuine strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal but belongs to the definition: these are the first teeth a child uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's first set of teeth are called milk teeth; choppers is slang for teeth.

clue.text: Finish transmitting without son

indicators.note: without means the son letter is taken away

parts.note: transmitting a message is sending it

explanation.surface: A broadcaster stops transmitting once the son is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the finish or conclusion of something.

clue.text: What comes after washing at university? Forgetting line!

parts.note: an actor who forgets a line is said to dry, so drying means forgetting a line
being up means being in residence at university

explanation.surface: A student actor, after doing the laundry, blanks on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Drying up is the chore after washing the dishes; 'at university' is the old British use of UP for being in residence at college.
explanation.definitionFit: After washing dishes, the next chore is wiping them dry, known in Britain as the drying up.

clue.text: Imagines Spanish that becomes attractive

parts.note: to picture something is to imagine it
que is the Spanish word for that

explanation.surface: A picture of Spanish scenery that turns out pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' is a link from wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Picturesque means visually charming, attractive like a painting.

clue.text: Married woman having to admit a complaint

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the married woman takes the letter in

parts.note: a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A wife is obliged to confess a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to admit' lets A into M LADY after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment, a synonym.

clue.text: Noises from animal in converted stables

definitions.meaning: the soft cries a cat or gull makes
a row of former stables turned into housing

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a mews is a street of stables converted into homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: cat cries are mews, and a mews is a stable yard turned to houses.

clue.text: Giving reasons for an outing planned to include two hundred

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the Roman numerals inside them
something planned is arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them are CC

explanation.surface: An excursion is organised to hold two hundred people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planned' rearranges AN OUTING to AOUNTING; 'to include' puts CC inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to explain it, so accounting for means giving reasons for it.

clue.text: Unable to speak, one copper gets delayed by fashionable painting

parts.note: something in is in fashion
painting is a form of art
I is the Roman numeral for one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
something delayed is late

explanation.surface: A policeman is left speechless when held up by a trendy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the element symbol CU; 'delayed by' only sets the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inarticulate cannot express themselves clearly in words.

clue.text: Radiation units finding information in damaged tensor

indicators.note: the information word goes inside the rearranged letters
damaged suggests the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Information found in a broken tensor gauge about radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TENSOR to ROENTS; 'in' puts GEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roentgen is an old unit measuring exposure to X-ray or gamma radiation.

clue.text: Point at which judge replaces pressure in flat tyre?

indicators.note: replaces means one letter swaps out another in the flat tyre word

parts.note: a puncture gives a flat tyre
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A judge decides where pressure gave out in a flat tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the flat tyre stands for PUNCTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A juncture is a particular point in time or in events.

clue.text: Last minute gives time for refreshments

definitions.meaning: the latest possible moment before it is too late
eleven in the morning, when the British break for a snack called elevenses

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is playful: the hour after ten is when elevenses, a British mid-morning snack, is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the latest possible moment, and literally names eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Elevate East German city over the French

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the city name is turned upside down

parts.note: Bonn is a city in Germany
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Raise up an eastern German city above the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses BONN to NNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, to elevate them in rank.

clue.text: Present wrapped in metal — where is it?

indicators.note: the present word is wrapped inside the metal word

parts.note: tin is a metal
to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A gift wrapped in foil, and someone asks where it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means being here, HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein means in that place, which is the answer to where is it.

clue.text: Planet's south leading a revolution

parts.note: a revolution is a turn

explanation.surface: A planet's southern side leads its rotation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; 'leading' just puts S first.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun.

clue.text: Question English on drink from French island

parts.note: a martini is a cocktail

explanation.surface: An English query about a cocktail served in a French territory.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so QU and E follow the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Martinique is a Caribbean island that is an overseas region of France.

clue.text: A people's competition

definitions.meaning: a group sharing descent, an ethnic group

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link joining the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Race means both an ethnic group of people and a contest of speed.

clue.text: Out of practice but reliable without leader

indicators.note: without leader means the first letter of the reliable word is dropped

parts.note: trusty means reliable

explanation.surface: A player is out of practice but still dependable, minus a captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty describes a skill gone stale from disuse, so out of practice.

clue.text: Excellent exercise runs in advance

indicators.note: the exercise and runs letters go inside the advance payment word

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages, British slang
PE is physical education, school exercise
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Excellent fitness training that gets you running ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A SUB is British for an advance on one's pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means of the highest quality, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Gets level nevertheless with putt, dropping point

parts.note: even so means nevertheless

indicators.note: the golf word loses the letters of the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: A golfer draws level anyway with a putt that falls at the right spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is not a compass letter here but PT; 'dropping' removes P and T from PUTT, leaving UT.
explanation.definitionFit: To even out is to become level or equal, so gets level is a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Made a home as requirement across street

indicators.note: the requirement word stretches across, around, the street abbreviation

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A housing need spanning a road led to settling in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that has nested has built a home, so the past tense matches made a home.

clue.text: Enemy failing to take west of zone is a catalyst

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the single letter from zone
failing suggests breaking down, so the letters are jumbled
in an across clue the west of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An enemy that fails to seize the western edge of a zone sparks a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges ENEMY to ENYME; 'to take' puts Z, from 'west of zone', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that speeds up a biochemical reaction, which is what a catalyst does.
